title: Baked Spaghetti Pie with Marinara and Mozzarella
description: An Italian-American way to turn a box of spaghetti, a few eggs and a can of tomatoes into sliceable wedges with a cheesy top. Dinner for four for about $10.
equipment: 10-inch oven-safe skillet or 9-inch deep pie plate
notes: The eggs and parmesan bind the noodles, so press the spaghetti down firmly and let the pie rest 10 minutes before cutting or the wedges will slump. Undercook the pasta by 2 minutes, since it keeps cooking in the oven. Sharp cheddar can stand in for half the mozzarella, and leftover cooked vegetables such as spinach or peppers can be folded into the noodles. To add meat, brown 1/2 lb ground beef to 160°F and stir it into the sauce. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and keep up to 4 days. Reheat wedges covered at 350°F for 15 minutes, or in the microwave, until they reach 165°F in the center. Wrapped wedges freeze for up to 2 months.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter (14 g), plus more for the pan
fresh basil leaves, torn, for serving

instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F with a rack in the center. Butter a 10-inch oven-safe skillet or a 9-inch deep pie plate. Bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it well.

Make the sauce while the water heats: warm the olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat, add the onion and a pinch of salt, and cook for 5 minutes until soft and translucent. Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the crushed tomatoes, oregano, red pepper flakes and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Simmer gently for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until slightly thickened.
Cook the spaghetti 2 minutes less than the package says, so it is still quite firm in the center. Drain well and return it to the warm pot. Toss with the butter until melted.
In a small bowl, beat the eggs with the parmesan, 1/2 teaspoon salt and several grinds of pepper. Pour over the spaghetti and toss with tongs until every strand is coated.

Transfer the spaghetti to the prepared pan and press it into an even layer with the back of a spoon, pushing it slightly up the sides to form a shallow crust. Spread about 1 1/2 cups of the sauce over the top and scatter the mozzarella evenly over the sauce.
Bake for 25 minutes, until the cheese is melted and spotted brown at the edges and the center feels set when pressed. The egg mixture should reach 160°F in the middle.
Let the pie rest for 10 minutes, then cut into 8 wedges. Rewarm the remaining sauce and spoon it over each serving, and scatter with basil if using.

title: Chilaquiles Rojos with Fried Eggs and Black Beans
description: Oven-crisped corn tortilla wedges tossed in a guajillo-tomato salsa, topped with fried eggs and served with black beans. A Mexican breakfast that makes an easy dinner for four for about $10.
notes: Stale tortillas crisp best, so this is a good use for the end of a package. Toss the chips with the salsa right before serving; after a few minutes they soften, which some families prefer and others do not. Guajillo chiles are mild and fruity; for more heat, add one dried chile de arbol or a pinch of cayenne to the blender. Skip the cheese and sour cream to make it dairy-free, or scramble the eggs instead of frying them for small children. The salsa keeps 5 days in the refrigerator or 3 months frozen, and the baked chips keep 3 days in an airtight bag. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours; assembled chilaquiles do not reheat well, so store the components separately and reheat the salsa and beans to 165°F.

ingredients.name: corn tortillas (6-inch), each cut into 6 wedges
dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
medium onion, roughly chopped, plus more finely chopped for serving
black beans (15 oz), with their liquid
full-fat sour cream, thinned with 1 tbsp water

instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Toss the tortilla wedges with 2 tablespoons of the oil and 1/4 teaspoon salt, spread them in a single layer on two rimmed baking sheets, and bake for 12 to 15 minutes, swapping the pans and flipping halfway, until golden and crisp. They crisp further as they cool.

While the chips bake, toast the guajillo chiles in a dry 12-inch skillet over medium heat for about 20 seconds per side, just until fragrant and slightly pliable; do not let them blacken or the salsa turns bitter. Put them in a small saucepan with the broth, bring to a simmer, then turn off the heat and let them soak for 10 minutes.
Pour the chiles and broth into a blender with the tomatoes and their juice, the roughly chopped onion, garlic, cumin, oregano and 3/4 teaspoon salt. Blend until completely smooth, about 1 minute.

Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon oil in the 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Pour in the salsa (it will spatter) and cook, stirring often, for 6 to 8 minutes, until it darkens to brick red and thickens enough to coat a spoon. Keep it warm over low heat.
Warm the black beans with their liquid in the small saucepan over medium-low heat, mashing a few against the side to thicken them, and season with a pinch of salt.

Fry the eggs in a lightly oiled nonstick skillet over medium heat in two batches, about 3 minutes, until the whites are fully set and the yolks are done to your liking. Season with the remaining salt.

Just before serving, add the chips to the salsa and fold gently for about 1 minute, until coated but still crisp at the edges. Divide among plates, scatter with the cheese and chopped onion, top each with two eggs, and serve with the beans, sour cream, cilantro and lime wedges.

title: Greek Baked Butter Beans (Gigantes-Style) with Tomato, Dill and Feta
description: Canned butter beans baked in a thick tomato, carrot and dill sauce until the top caramelizes, finished with crumbled feta. Hearty, meatless, and dinner for four for about $10.
notes: Gigantes are usually made from dried giant beans; canned butter beans get you most of the way in under an hour. The sauce should look loose going into the oven and jammy coming out; if it dries before the top browns, splash in a little water. Serve with crusty bread or pita for dipping (this adds wheat), or over rice to keep it gluten-free. Leave off the feta for a vegan, dairy-free dish, or use cannellini beans if butter beans are hard to find. The flavor improves overnight, and leftovers are good at room temperature as a lunch. Refrigerate within 2 hours and keep up to 5 days; reheat covered to 165°F. The beans freeze well without the feta for up to 3 months.

ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
butter beans (15 oz each), drained and rinsed

instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F with a rack in the center.

Warm the olive oil in a 12-inch oven-safe skillet over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot and celery with a pinch of salt and cook, stirring occasionally, for 8 to 10 minutes, until soft and just starting to turn golden. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, until it darkens slightly. Add the crushed tomatoes, water, oregano, cinnamon, sugar, salt and several grinds of pepper. Simmer for 5 minutes.

Fold in the butter beans and half the dill, taking care not to break the beans. The sauce should just cover them; add a splash more water if it looks thick. If you are using a baking dish, transfer everything to it now.
Drizzle the top with a little more olive oil and bake uncovered for 30 to 35 minutes, until the sauce is thick and bubbling and the beans on top are browned and slightly crisp at the edges.
Scatter the feta and the remaining dill over the top and let the dish rest for 5 minutes. Serve warm with lemon wedges.

title: Vegetable Egg Foo Young with Brown Gravy and Jasmine Rice
description: Chinese-American takeout-style omelet patties packed with bean sprouts, cabbage and scallions, under a quick soy gravy with rice. Dinner for four for about $9.
notes: Dry the sprouts and cabbage well; wet vegetables make the patties steam and fall apart. Keep the oil hot enough that the egg puffs and sizzles at the edges the moment it hits the pan. Leftover cooked chicken, pork or shrimp can be chopped and added to the batter (shrimp adds shellfish and none of these are vegetarian). Use gluten-free tamari in the gravy for a gluten-free version. Refrigerate patties, gravy and rice separately within 2 hours and keep up to 3 days. Reheat patties in a skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes per side and the gravy until simmering, so both reach 165°F. They do not freeze well.

ingredients.name: mung bean sprouts, rinsed and patted dry
scallions, thinly sliced, white and green parts separated
cornstarch, stirred into 3 tbsp cold water

instructions: Combine the rice with 2 1/4 cups water and 1/4 teaspoon salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, cover, reduce the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Turn off the heat and let it steam, still covered, for 10 minutes.

Make the gravy: bring the broth, soy sauce and sugar to a simmer in a small saucepan over medium heat. Stir the cornstarch mixture again, pour it in while stirring, and simmer for 1 minute until glossy and thick enough to coat a spoon. Stir in the sesame oil, cover and keep warm over the lowest heat.

In a large bowl, beat the eggs with the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and the pepper until no streaks of white remain. Add the bean sprouts, cabbage, carrot, scallion whites and peas and stir until everything is coated.

Heat 1 1/2 tablespoons of the oil in a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Using a 1/3-cup measure, scoop the mixture into the pan to make 3 patties, nudging stray vegetables back into each round with a spatula.

Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until the edges are puffed and deep golden, then flip carefully and cook 2 minutes more, until the center is set and springs back when pressed. Move to a plate and repeat with the remaining oil and mixture to make about 10 patties.
Serve the patties over the rice with the warm gravy spooned on top and the scallion greens scattered over.

title: Southern Smothered Chicken Thighs with Onion Gravy and Rice
description: Seasoned chicken thighs browned, then simmered under a peppery onion gravy until tender, spooned over white rice. Southern Sunday flavor on a weeknight, dinner for four for about $10.
notes: The browned bits left in the pan after searing the chicken are what give the gravy its color, so do not wash the skillet between steps. Cook the onions until truly golden; pale onions make a pale, flat gravy. Bone-in, skin-on thighs work too and cost even less per pound; brown them skin side down for 6 minutes and simmer 30 to 35 minutes. Serve with green beans or collards and a dash of hot sauce. Refrigerate within 2 hours and keep up to 4 days; reheat covered over low heat with a splash of broth until the chicken reaches 165°F. The chicken and gravy freeze well for up to 3 months.
instructions: Pat the chicken dry. Mix 1 teaspoon of the salt with the paprika, garlic powder and pepper and rub it over both sides of the thighs. Put the flour in a shallow dish and dredge each thigh, shaking off the excess. Save the leftover flour.

Start the rice: combine it with 2 1/4 cups water and the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt in a medium saucepan, bring to a boil, cover, reduce the heat to low and cook for 18 minutes. Let it stand covered off the heat until the chicken is ready.
Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken in a single layer for 4 minutes per side, until deep golden; it will not be cooked through yet. Move it to a plate.

Reduce the heat to medium and add the butter, onions and a pinch of salt. Cook, scraping up the browned bits, for 10 to 12 minutes, until the onions are soft and golden brown. Add the garlic and thyme and cook for 1 minute.
Sprinkle 2 tablespoons of the reserved flour over the onions and stir for 1 minute. Slowly pour in the broth, stirring constantly, and bring to a simmer; the gravy will thicken as it bubbles.

Return the chicken and any juices to the skillet, spooning gravy and onions over the top. Cover and simmer gently over medium-low heat for 15 to 18 minutes, until the chicken is tender and reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer. Stir in the hot sauce and taste for salt.
Fluff the rice with a fork and serve the chicken and plenty of onion gravy over it, sprinkled with parsley.

title: Home-Style Chicken and Potato Curry (Aloo Murgh) with Basmati Rice
description: An everyday North Indian-style curry where potatoes stretch a pound and a half of chicken thighs to feed four, simmered in an onion-tomato masala. Dinner for four for about $10.
equipment: Dutch oven or heavy 5-quart pot with lid
notes: Take your time browning the onions; deep golden onions are what make the gravy rich without cream. This version is mild enough for most children; add a minced green chile or more cayenne at the table for anyone who wants heat. Ghee in place of oil adds a buttery flavor and adds milk, and a spoonful of plain yogurt stirred in at the end does the same. Cauliflower florets or frozen peas can stand in for some of the potato. Refrigerate within 2 hours and keep up to 4 days; reheat covered with a splash of water until the chicken reaches 165°F. The curry freezes well for 3 months, though the potatoes soften a little.

ingredients.name: basmati rice (300 g), rinsed until the water runs clear
boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
russet or yukon gold potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch chunks

instructions: Combine the rice with 2 1/4 cups water and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, cover, reduce the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it covered until serving.

Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for about 20 seconds, until a shade darker and fragrant. Add the onions and cook, stirring often, for 12 to 15 minutes, until evenly golden brown.

Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute. Stir in the turmeric, coriander, paprika and cayenne for 30 seconds, then add the crushed tomatoes and 1 teaspoon salt. Cook, stirring and scraping the bottom, for 6 to 8 minutes, until the masala thickens and oil shimmers at the edges.
Add the chicken and stir to coat it in the masala. Cook for 3 minutes, until the outside turns opaque. Add the potatoes, water and remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and bring to a boil.

Cover, reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for 18 to 20 minutes, stirring once or twice, until a knife slides easily through the potatoes and the chicken reads 165°F. If the gravy is thin, simmer uncovered for a few minutes more.
Stir in the garam masala, taste for salt, and scatter with cilantro. Fluff the rice with a fork and serve the curry over it.

title: Korean-Inspired Spicy Pork and Cabbage Stir-Fry (Jeyuk Bokkeum Style)
description: Thin slices of inexpensive pork shoulder in a sweet, garlicky gochujang sauce, stir-fried with plenty of cabbage and onion and served over rice. Dinner for four for about $10.
notes: Freeze the pork for 30 minutes before slicing so you can cut it into thin, even pieces; thin slices cook through in minutes. Pork shoulder is cheaper and juicier than loin, and the cabbage stretches 1 1/4 pounds to four generous plates. For children, halve the gochujang and skip the red pepper flakes, then pass extra gochujang at the table. Most gochujang contains wheat and soy; look for a gluten-free brand and use gluten-free tamari if you need it. Whole cuts of pork are safe at 145°F, and these thin slices pass that quickly once they lose all their pink. Refrigerate within 2 hours and keep up to 3 days; reheat in a skillet until steaming and 165°F.

ingredients.name: boneless pork shoulder, trimmed and sliced 1/8 inch thick
medium yellow onion, sliced into thin half-moons
green cabbage, cut into 1-inch pieces (about 1/2 small head)
carrot, peeled and thinly sliced on the diagonal

instructions: Combine the rice with 2 cups water and 1/4 teaspoon salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, cover, reduce the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes, then let it steam off the heat, covered, for 10 minutes.

In a mixing bowl, stir together the gochujang, soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, sesame oil and red pepper flakes. Add the sliced pork and massage the sauce into it until every piece is coated. Let it sit for 10 minutes while you cut the vegetables.

Heat 1 tablespoon of the neutral oil in a wok or 12-inch skillet over high heat until it shimmers. Add the onion, carrot, cabbage and the remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt and stir-fry for 4 to 5 minutes, until the cabbage is wilted at the edges but still has some crunch. Tip onto a plate.

Add the remaining tablespoon of oil to the pan over high heat. Add the pork in a single layer with all its marinade and let it sear undisturbed for 1 minute, then stir-fry for 4 to 6 minutes more, until no pink remains and the sauce is sticky and lightly caramelized at the edges. Lower the heat slightly if the sauce starts to scorch.
Return the vegetables to the pan with the scallions and toss for 1 minute to coat everything in sauce and heat through.
Serve over the rice, sprinkled with sesame seeds.

title: Ground Turkey Calabacitas Tacos with Zucchini and Corn
description: A Mexican-style skillet of zucchini, corn and fire-roasted tomatoes with seasoned ground turkey, piled into warm corn tortillas. Half the filling is vegetables, so one pound feeds four for about $10.
notes: Cut the zucchini into small, even dice so it browns rather than steams; a crowded pan makes the filling watery. For children who dislike heat, leave out the jalapeño and add it to the adults' tacos at the table. Crumbled cheese or sour cream on top is traditional and adds milk. Ground beef works in place of turkey; cook it to 160°F and pour off excess fat. The filling also makes a good rice bowl or quesadilla filling the next day. Refrigerate within 2 hours and keep up to 4 days, reheating to 165°F; the filling freezes for 3 months.

ingredients.name: fire-roasted diced tomatoes (15 oz), with their juice

instructions: Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add the turkey and press it into an even layer; cook undisturbed for 3 minutes, until browned underneath, then break it into small crumbles.

Add the onion, jalapeño, garlic, chili powder, cumin, oregano and 3/4 teaspoon salt. Cook, stirring, for 4 minutes, until the onion softens and the turkey is no longer pink. Move everything to the edges of the pan.

Add the zucchini and corn to the center with the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and cook without stirring for 2 minutes so the zucchini picks up some color, then stir everything together and cook 2 minutes more.

Pour in the tomatoes and their juice and simmer for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until most of the liquid has cooked off and the zucchini is tender but holds its shape. Check that the turkey reads 165°F, and taste for salt.

While the filling simmers, warm the tortillas one at a time in a dry skillet or directly over a gas flame for about 30 seconds per side, until soft and lightly charred, stacking them in a clean towel to stay warm.
Spoon the filling into the tortillas, top with cilantro, and serve with lime wedges for squeezing.

title: One-Pot Beef and Ditalini with Tomatoes and Peas
description: Italian-American comfort in one pot: small pasta cooked right in a beefy tomato sauce with carrots and peas, finished with parmesan. Three-quarters of a pound of beef makes dinner for four for about $10.
notes: Stir often once the pasta goes in, scraping the bottom, because the starch and tomatoes can stick. The pasta keeps absorbing liquid as it sits, so it should look a little loose when you take it off the heat. Small elbows or small shells can replace ditalini, and ground turkey works in place of beef if cooked to 165°F. Leave out the parmesan for a dairy-free pot. Refrigerate within 2 hours and keep up to 4 days; reheat with a splash of water or broth until it reaches 165°F. It freezes for up to 2 months, though the pasta softens.

ingredients.name: finely grated parmesan cheese (45 g), plus more for serving

instructions: Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the beef and cook, breaking it into small pieces, for 5 to 6 minutes, until browned and no longer pink; it should reach 160°F. Spoon off all but about 1 tablespoon of fat.
Add the onion and carrot and cook, stirring, for 5 minutes, until the onion is soft. Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, oregano and red pepper flakes and cook for 1 minute, until the paste darkens.
Add the crushed tomatoes, broth, water and salt, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Bring to a boil.

Stir in the ditalini, reduce the heat to medium so the pot bubbles steadily, and cook uncovered for 11 to 13 minutes, stirring every minute or two, until the pasta is tender and the sauce has thickened. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick before the pasta is done.
Stir in the peas and cook for 2 minutes until hot. Take the pot off the heat, stir in the parmesan, and season with pepper and more salt if needed.
Let it stand for 3 minutes, then serve in bowls topped with basil and extra parmesan.

title: Louisiana-Style Red Beans and Rice with Bacon
description: Canned kidney beans simmered with bacon, the onion-pepper-celery trinity, thyme and smoked paprika until creamy, spooned over white rice. A Southern Monday supper, dinner for four for about $9.
notes: Mashing part of the beans against the pot is what turns the liquid creamy, so do not skip it. Three slices of bacon flavor the whole pot; for a vegetarian version, cook the vegetables in 3 tablespoons of oil, add an extra 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika, and use vegetable broth. If you have smoked sausage, slice 8 ounces and brown it with the bacon. To cook from dried beans, simmer 1 pound of soaked red kidney beans for about 1 1/2 hours in place of the cans; it is cheaper still. Refrigerate within 2 hours and keep up to 5 days; the beans thicken as they sit, so loosen them with water and reheat to 165°F. The beans freeze for up to 3 months.

ingredients.name: red kidney beans (15 oz each), drained and rinsed
louisiana-style cayenne pepper hot sauce, plus more for serving

instructions: Cook the bacon in a Dutch oven over medium heat, stirring occasionally, for 6 to 8 minutes, until the fat has rendered and the bacon is crisp. Leave the bacon and fat in the pot.

Add the onion, bell pepper and celery and cook, stirring, for 8 minutes, until soft and lightly browned. Add the garlic, thyme, smoked paprika, cayenne and bay leaves and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the beans, broth, 1 teaspoon salt and the pepper. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer uncovered for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally.

Meanwhile, combine the rice with 2 1/4 cups water and the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, cover, reduce the heat to low and cook for 18 minutes, then let it stand covered off the heat.

Using a potato masher or the back of a spoon, crush about a third of the beans against the side of the pot and stir them in. Simmer 5 minutes more, until the liquid is thick and creamy. Remove the bay leaves, stir in the hot sauce, and taste for salt.
Spoon the beans over the rice, scatter with scallions, and pass more hot sauce at the table.
